[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Spartanburg, South Carolina facility (internal code SPA01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 5700 N Blackstock Rd, Spartanburg, SC 29303.

reading.body:
DartPoints Spartanburg publishes 0.8 MW of IT capacity. At 10 kW per rack, a common edge-colocation density, that is roughly 80 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 20 racks. The arithmetic is an illustration of scale, not an operator claim. No certifications are published on the spec page read for this site, so no certification-based judgments about what workloads the campus qualifies to host can be made.

The 0.8 MW figure places this campus fourth among the four South Carolina facilities that publish a megawatt figure at all, out of 14 facilities mapped in the state. Those four facilities together publish 6.6 MW total, meaning Spartanburg accounts for roughly 12 percent of that published South Carolina figure. Most mapped facilities in South Carolina publish no capacity figure, so the statewide total visible to this site is a floor, not a census.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the honest answer the published data supports is: not at the scale of AI training. A facility under 1 MW sits below the threshold where large-scale GPU clusters are practical, because a single modern AI training pod of 512 accelerators can draw that entire budget on its own. The campus is sized for edge inference, regional connectivity, or enterprise colocation, none of which are disqualifying for AI at the right workload size, but it is not a candidate for the hyperscale or frontier-model training conversations this site tracks as grid-constrained.
